To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed two new plasmids for the expression of cloned genes in E. coli cells.
we constructed new plasmids pMl2.1 and PML4 for the cloning of regulatory regions.
the plasmids pM12.1 and pM14 were constructed for cloning transcription regulatory regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of vectors for the study of the transcription regulatory regions in E. coli cells.
the construction of vectors for cloning of transcription regulatory regions and their expression in E. coli.
the construction of new plasmids for the cloning of foreign regulatory regions and the expression of genes controlled by them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new vectors are very useful tools for the study of transcription regulation and for cloning of transcription regulatory regions.
the pML2 and pML4 are useful vectors for cloning of transcription regulatory regions.
the pML2 and pML4 plasmids are useful for the cloning of foreign regulatory regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the foreign transcription regulatory regions can be cloned in the pML plasmids and expressed in the E. coli K12 cells, and the pML4 is suitable for the cloning of the transcription regulatory elements.
the pML2 and pML4 plasmids are useful for cloning transcription regulatory regions and their effectivity was tested by cloning the lacUV5 and the trpL promoter regions.
the foreign regulatory elements can be expressed in E. coli cells and the pML plasmids are convenient for cloning of the regulatory regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
these vectors are very suitable for the construction of the transcriptional regulatory systems in E. coli cells.
the pML plasmids can be used for the cloning of the transcription regulatory regions.
pML2. 1 and pML.4 plasmids are suitable for cloning of transcription regulatory regions.
